The existing :mod:`tooling.providers.steam_install` boundary can safely ask
Windows to open ``steam://install/<appid>``.  Valve does not document that URI
as proof that a download started, however, and an install-looking surface may
instead be a store, purchase, licence or subscription surface.  This module
therefore adds a deliberately separate PREPARE/COMMIT protocol:
* PREPARE authenticates AppID/title metadata, pre-seals every navigation
outcome, asks a trusted navigator to open the URI, then asks an independent
observer to scan the current Steam UI **without receiving the request**.

title, byte counts, library, free space and one exact InvokePattern control
can mint an opaque, short-lived, one-use commit handle and human review;

one final atomic revalidation/InvokePattern request to the trusted backend.

ownership, download start or installation.  The existing manifest/content-log
verifier remains the sole STARTED/INSTALLED authority.  This experimental

head: """Experimental fail-closed Windows observations for Steam installation.
This module is intentionally not registered as a BAXY tool.  It supplies the
read-only observations consumed by :mod:`tooling.providers.steam_install` and
keeps discovery separate from entitlement and catalog authority:
* Registry values discover a candidate Steam root and URI handler only.
* ``libraryfolders.vdf``, app manifests, ``content_log.txt``, ``appinfo`` and
``loginusers.vdf`` never prove ownership or an authenticated account.
* ``authenticated_session=True`` is emitted only when an injected authority
verifies an account/session binding to the exact PID and process creation
time observed by psutil.
* Every filesystem path is drive-absolute and local.  UNC, device namespaces,
alternate data streams, traversal, DOS devices, reparse points and ambiguous
identities fail closed.
This adapter does not claim that ``steam://install/<appid>`` starts a download;
Valve does not publish that postcondition.  It may only open an install dialog.
The product path remains experimental until a live Windows matrix establishes
the dialog behavior and a separate UIA phase can verify AppID/title/size/library,
exclude purchase surfaces, request confirmation, and press the exact install
control.  Manifest/content-log observations prove only what happened afterward.
There is deliberately no built-in ownership adapter.  Steamworks
``CheckAppOwnership`` requires a publisher Web API key and Valve says publisher
keys must never be shipped to clients.  Client ``BIsSubscribedApp`` requires a
legitimate Steamworks application context, which BAXY does not have.  Therefore
ownership must arrive through the separately injected/authenticated entitlement
authority used by ``SteamInstallPreflightService``; otherwise the action stops.
The default adapter uses Win32 handles, ``winreg``, psutil and the stable,
double-read parsers in :mod:`tooling.providers.steam`.  Construction performs
no I/O; all probes are bounded, cancellable and read-only.
Primary references checked 2026-07-12:
